t.E472c.agn: In 2020 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and found no safety concern at the reported use levels. In its 2025 follow-up opinion, EFSA also found no safety concern at the reported and maximum permitted levels in formulae for infants below 16 weeks of age.
t.E472c.body: During digestion in the body it is largely broken down into glycerol, fatty acids and the corresponding organic acid (citric acid); these are used like the fats in foods.
t.E472c.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E472c.prod: It is an emulsifier produced by esterification of glycerol with citric acid and fatty acids, or of mono- and diglycerides with citric acid.
t.E472c.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed, no safety concern.
t.E472c.regx.1: Follow-up opinion: no safety concern for use in foods for infants below 16 weeks of age; specification update recommended.
t.E472c.summary: An emulsifier derived from mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids. It improves texture in bread, cake and margarine; the fat source may be vegetable or animal.
t.E472c.what: As an emulsifier, it helps oil and water mix and prevents spattering.
